title: The 3N71B gets ATF Type F, as the factory specifies; the Dexron VI bought is not for this box
body:
**D-365 — The 3N71B gets ATF Type F, as the factory specifies; the Dexron VI bought is not for this box.** Camden's call, 2026-09-21, answering `CAR.01`: **"a"**. Closes `CAR.01`.

**The ruling.** Mazda specifies ATF Type F (Ford M2C33-F) for the 1982 3N71B automatic (`specs` SP-093, sources S-002 p.0-24 and S-003). Type F has no friction modifier. Dexron-family fluids soften this box's shifts and can make its bands slip, and there is no record of a rebuild with modern friction material that would allow them. So Type F goes in. The Valvoline Dexron VI / Mercon LV already bought (PH045, not fitted) is not used in this transmission: keep it for something else or return it.

**Why this is a decision in `00-CAR`.** It's a car-level service call, not part of any project, and `00-CAR` had no decisions table. One was added in this run so car-level rulings have a home. `00-CAR`'s fact tables still never cite a decision (§6.6, enforced by `check`): they state what the car takes, and this body says why.

**In the data.** `intervals` atf: spec is ATF Type F, and the "owner rules which" note is gone. `parts_history` PH045 marked "NOT for this transmission"; PH053 added, Type F to buy, 6.2 L for a full refill (SP-094). `specs` SP-147 folded into SP-094 (they were duplicates; SP-147 was kept only while this block cited it). New `00-CAR` table `decisions` (with `_tables` and `_schema` rows).

title: The oil metering pump is disconnected; the engine runs on premix in the fuel
body:
**D-366 — The oil metering pump is disconnected; the engine runs on premix in the fuel.** Camden's call, 2026-09-21, answering `CAR.02`: **"b"**. Closes `CAR.02`.

**The fact.** Option (b) of the block: "It's disconnected and the car runs on premix (2-stroke oil in the fuel)". On the 12A the oil metering pump fed engine oil into the factory carburettor to lubricate the apex seals (SP-024). The carburettor went with the Weber conversion (M-001), and the pump is disconnected. The apex seals now get their oil only from two-stroke oil mixed into the fuel.

**What it means.** Premix goes in at **every** fill-up, without exception. A tank without it runs the seals dry. That is now a service interval, not a habit.

**Still unknown.** The **ratio** isn't recorded anywhere. It's marked `confirm` in `intervals` premix and `mods` M-013. Camden knows it; it goes into those two rows the next time he says what he mixes. Also unknown is when the pump was disconnected (with the Weber, or after).

**In the data.** `as_fitted` Engine; `mods` M-013 (new); `intervals` premix (new, every fill); `specs` SP-024's note (the factory design, and what this car does instead).

title: The free CAD library, and one combined model of the FB built from it
body:
# The free CAD library, and one combined model of the FB built from it

*2026-09-25 - Camden, in chat*

**Decision.**
- **Every free 3D model, scan and dimensioned drawing found** for the FB, its parts, the 12A and 13B, the LS/CD009 swap and the electrical project's parts is catalogued in `01-REFERENCE` table `cad`, one row each: 891 rows, 315 of them on this PC. The other 576 need an account (GrabCAD, Sketchfab, SnapEDA, Thingiverse through a browser) and keep their links, so he can fetch any of them by hand.
- **The files live in `01-REFERENCE/model/library/`** beside the bought SA model (S-037), and stay out of git like it: the repository is public and the licences vary (CC-BY, CC-BY-NC, 3D Warehouse, manufacturer terms). `model/catalog.py` imports the finders' manifests into `cad`; once imported, the row is the fact's home.
- **One combined model**, `01-REFERENCE/model/out/rx7-fb.blend` and `.glb`, is built by `model/blend.py` in one frame (mm, x right, y forward, z up, ground z = 0, front axle y = 0). Each piece is a `blend` row naming its source, its fit and the factory figure that checks it. Shown: the FB shell, wheels built from the specs, the 12A, the FB tail lamps. Hidden overlays: the SA body (detail) and an LS3 (the swap's envelope).
- **The factory underbody figures on S-002 p.14-24** that could be checked by arithmetic are 00-CAR specs SP-234 to SP-240. The pairings on that page that could not be read without doubt are left on the page, not guessed.

**His words.**
> please do a verry thurrough search for free 3dCAD models of the FB rx7 and of its parts, or any of the parts listed in any of the projects, find any and all douplicates are okay for better overall design and verification. please mafe a folder for all these files, store any and every cad file, then please review and prossess them all into a blend of parts and details, mayne even get 13b or other similar parts for 3D reference. when you have found everything you can please process each to one true model and or fact sheed for the 3d representation of the car, then tell me what you found and how your picture of the car improved

**Readings taken.**
- **"A folder for all these files".** `01-REFERENCE/model/library/`, not a new top-level folder: reference material belongs to 01-REFERENCE (R10), and `model/` already held the one 3D model. A folder named `cad/` was tried first and refused by `check`: the cad/ fence belongs to the KiCad boards.
- **"Fact sheet".** There are no pages (D-405). The fact sheet is the record: `cad` (what exists), `blend` (what the one model is made of, and how well each piece agrees with the factory), and SP-234 to SP-240.
- **"One true model".** Where two sources disagree, the factory figure wins, and every model is scaled or placed to it; the model's own error against the factory is written into `blend.check`. Nothing about the real car is measured from any model (R11). The 12A's position in the bay is an assumption, one line in `blend.py`, until the car is apart.
- **Out of git.** The same reading as D-415: reversible by one line in `.gitignore`.

**What the checks found.**
- The free FB shell (3D Warehouse, "1983 Mazda RX7"), scaled to the factory length, is 1682 mm wide without mirrors (factory 1669, +0.8 %) and its arches sit 2432 mm apart (factory wheelbase 2420, +0.5 %). Its right tail lamp is 480.1 mm long; an independent 1:1 scan of the real housing (Printables 993677) is 479.1 mm. Three independent agreements: the shell's proportions are right.
- The 12A's housing width, 70.02 mm, is derived from its 573 cc per rotor (SP-010) on the shared 105 / 15 mm trochoid, never typed. The 13B model's housings are 80.0 mm (the 13B's own) and its rotor matches a separate full-size 13B rotor to 1 mm.
- The bought SA model is 3.4 % wide at the tyre centres against the factory track.

**Consequences.** `01-REFERENCE`: tables `cad` and `blend` (new), `model/catalog.py`, `model/blend.py`, `model/README.md`. `00-CAR`: specs SP-234 to SP-240. `.gitignore`: `model/library/` and `model/out/`. Nothing in the app changes: its 3D view still loads the SA (D-415); moving it to the FB shell is a separate choice.

title: Every part's factory Mazda number and catalogue page, from the 1981-83 parts catalogue
body:
# Every part's factory Mazda number and catalogue page, from the 1981-83 parts catalogue

*2026-09-25 - Camden, in chat; read by the agent from S-005*

**Decision.**
- **00-CAR `parts` gains `oem_no`** (the factory part's Mazda number for a 1982 US automatic, from S-005) **and `catalogue`** (the file, PDF page and figure where S-005 shows it, with its exploded drawing). They are the catalogue's facts, not a claim about what is fitted now: that stays `part_no`.
- **40 parts** have both, read with high confidence. The part pages can show the factory drawing (the catalogue page) beside the part, and a replacement can be ordered by number.
- **`support`** is filled for 55 parts (the maker's or the main supplier's line: Mazdatrix 562-426-7960, Atkins Rotary 360-832-1990, Pierce Manifolds, Holley), and **`link`** for 18 more, each a supplier page for a 1982 RX-7 (RockAuto's catalogue by system). Bare supplier home pages were not stored: `support` already names the supplier.

**His words.**
> now scour all other things and ways you think we can represent information about this car. this should ait the model that is makeing the manual

**How it was read.** A research agent used the fiche's own alphabetical index (Body-Index PDF pp.133-146) and each page's frame code, and for every part gave the figure, the page and the applicability (year, market, transmission, chassis range). Two were checked by hand against the page: PT020 radiator N202-15-310B (A/T; M/T is N201-15-310B), S-005 Engine-Chassis p.46, 1500A-1; PT033 retractor motors FA01-51-931B (R) and FA01-51-941B (L), Body-Index p.33, 5103A-1. Both match.

**Not stored - medium or low readings, which need a second look before anything is bought:**
- PT001 12A rotary engine: read as N232-02-000 (low) - Scan of the assembly table is badly degraded; the N23x-02-000 pattern is legible, the exact digits are a best reading. Catalogue notes complete assemblies are s
- PT010 Fuel cut-off: read as 3919-45-170A (medium) - The factory part is a rollover/cut valve in the fuel line; the fitted item is an aftermarket unit (record links Amazon B0C2QJ1518) - they may not be the same fu
- PT011 Fuel line, 3/8 in: read as 9935-80-8999 (medium) - Factory bulk hose numbers by size code; fitted line is aftermarket 3/8 in.
- PT012 Vacuum lines and fittings: read as 9935-10-4999 (low) - Bulk hose numbers only; the fitted set is aftermarket (Amazon kit).
- PT017 Spark plug wires: read as 0000-18-097B (medium) - Set number is clear. Individual leads: 1480-18-130B, 1480-18-160A, 1480-18-170B, 8871-18-180A; 18140/18150 also cite 0000-18-097B. Which D-code is which plug le
- PT018 Coil wires: read as 8248-18-110 (low) - Assumed to be the two coil-to-distributor leads from their D-codes (18110/18120, next to the coils); confirm against the illustration. Also covered by set 0000-
- PT021 Water pump: read as 1757-23-920G (medium) - Clearly printed, but the '-23-' group is unusual for a water pump; confirm with a supplier before ordering. Gasket 1757-15-132; water baffle plate for '82 from 
- PT024 Battery: read as 0000-80-124K (medium) - Mazda-branded replacement battery number; any group-size battery of the right capacity fits (record SP-059: 55 Ah for Federal A/T).
- PT027 Wiring harness: read as FA30-67-010D (low) - Front-harness digit is partly obscured (FA30-67-0?0D); no '82 line printed past chassis 622565 - check the VIN. The harness is not bought new; this is for ident
- PT029 Interval wiper control unit: read as FA02-67-540 (low) - No separate intermittent-wiper amplifier was found in the fiche. FA02-67-540 is the only dash wiper control listed; column switch BA30-66-123 is also a wiper sw
- PT030 Hatch release solenoid: read as FA01-62-310C (medium) - The fiche gives no separate solenoid part; the power-opener lock is sold whole.
- PT036 Rear defrost switch: read as B001-66-460 (medium) - First character read as 'B' (the 8/B shapes are close on this scan).
- PT040 A/C system: read as 0000-67-1265-57 (medium) - The compressor number was not read (the section continues on later pages). Parts for this dealer kit are now largely unobtainable new.
- PT056 Front struts and coil springs: read as FA01-34-910B (medium) - The R spring prints as 'F001' and the L as 'FA01' - clearly printed, may be a real R/L difference or a fiche typo; confirm before ordering.

Two of those wait on the VIN (00-CAR vehicle row `vin`, not yet read): the '82 harness line stops at chassis FB331..622565, and several numbers change at a chassis number.

**Correction to D-421.** Its body says 20 parts are placed; the count is 18 (7 by the models, 11 at the wheel centres).

**Consequences.** 00-CAR `_schema` (`parts.oem_no`, `parts.catalogue`) and `parts`: oem_no and catalogue on 40 rows, support on 55, link on 18.
